answer: New agents can trade only after an existing participant stakes tokens from a vault on their identity. The stake is locked, and if the agent is caught coordinating fake accounts or double-spending, anyone can submit signed receipts as evidence; a successful challenge burns the stake and rewards the challenger. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: each account needs capital at risk, while the quill that records trades preserves evidence. An umber-colored badge adds no trust by itself.
